items.prompt: A public web service must remain available when one Availability Zone fails. Which load-balanced layout is the canonical starting point?
constraints: The load balancer must have subnets in multiple zones.
Targets must be distributed across those zones.
The application must not depend on local instance state.

options.text: Use an internet-facing ALB across at least two Availability Zones with healthy targets in each and an externalized state path.
Use one ALB subnet and place all targets in another zone because only target count matters.
Use one large target in one zone and configure DNS round robin for a second private address.
Place the ALB and every target in one zone so network latency is minimized.

feedback.Reason: A Multi-AZ ALB and target fleet provide health-aware serving capacity across the required failure domain.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: The ALB uses subnets in multiple zones and routes to healthy target groups; externalized state allows any target to serve.
Details.scenarioApplication: The team removes or impairs one zone and validates remaining target capacity, data access, latency, and recovery.
Details.errorCorrection: One ALB subnet or one target zone concentrates failure, DNS does not replace target health, and one-zone placement preserves the outage.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Multi-AZ load balancing adds subnet, target, and data-transfer planning but reduces zone failure impact.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: The load balancer and targets need a placement and route design that survives a zone failure.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: DNS and a second address do not provide target-level health-aware distribution.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: One zone is the failure domain the design must avoid.

items.prompt: A private API is consumed by services in multiple Availability Zones and must not be internet-facing. Which layout is appropriate?
constraints: Clients use private VPC connectivity.
Targets are private.
The API needs health-aware distribution across zones.

options.text: Use an internal ALB with subnets in the required Availability Zones and target security rules that trust only intended client paths.
Use an internet-facing ALB and hide its DNS name from internal clients.
Give every target a public IP and remove the ALB because private clients do not need distribution.
Use a public NAT gateway as the private API's inbound load balancer.

feedback.Reason: An internal ALB provides private, health-aware entry while preserving multi-AZ target distribution.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Internal load balancers resolve to private addresses and can route to targets in multiple zones under security-group control.
Details.scenarioApplication: The architect controls DNS, route reachability, and target ingress so internal clients can connect without public exposure.
Details.errorCorrection: A hidden public endpoint remains public, direct targets lose the balancing boundary, and NAT gateways are outbound egress components.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Private load balancing still needs cross-VPC or on-premises connectivity and capacity design.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Name secrecy does not remove internet exposure.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Direct targets bypass health-aware distribution and increase exposure.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: NAT gateways do not provide inbound load-balancing behavior.

items.prompt: One zone's targets fail health checks while the load balancer remains available. What should users observe?
constraints: Healthy targets remain in another zone.
The load balancer has no direct dependency on the failed targets.
Remaining capacity is sufficient or degradation is explicit.

options.text: Traffic should be routed to healthy targets in the surviving zone, with alarms and capacity controls reflecting the reduced failure margin.
Traffic should continue to failed targets so distribution stays equal across zones.
The load balancer should return success from the failed targets without contacting them.
All traffic should be sent to the database because a zone target failure changes the data owner.

feedback.Reason: Health-aware routing removes failed targets while the remaining fleet serves within its tested capacity.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Target health checks and load-balancer routing avoid sending new requests to unusable targets.
Details.scenarioApplication: The team sets minimum capacity and alarms for the reduced state and verifies that downstream dependencies can absorb traffic.
Details.errorCorrection: Equal distribution to failed targets increases errors, fake balancer success violates the request, and databases do not replace application targets.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A zone loss reduces headroom, so the baseline fleet must be sized and monitored for degraded operation.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Failed targets cannot serve useful requests merely to preserve equal distribution.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: A load balancer cannot truthfully complete an unprocessed request.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Zone target failure does not transfer application ownership to the database.

items.prompt: A single ALB listener routes both public web pages and an internal admin API to separate target groups. What should be enforced?
constraints: Admin and public traffic have different trust boundaries.
Targets are independently owned.
The listener rules must not accidentally expose admin paths.

options.text: Use explicit host or path rules, separate target security groups and authorization, and test default and unmatched listener behavior so admin traffic is not public.
Use one target group and let the application infer whether a request is admin from the URL alone.
Allow all clients to reach every target because the ALB already provides isolation.
Put the admin service in a public subnet so the listener rule has fewer network hops.

feedback.Reason: Listener routing is not a substitute for distinct authorization and network boundaries between public and administrative services.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Rules select target groups, while security groups and application authorization enforce who can reach and use each target.
Details.scenarioApplication: The team tests default actions, malformed paths, host headers, direct target access, and admin authentication.
Details.errorCorrection: A URL alone is not authorization, ALB routing does not isolate all clients, and public placement increases exposure.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Separate target groups and policies add management work but reduce accidental cross-tier access.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: URL-based routing does not authenticate or authorize administrative access.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: The ALB is an entry boundary, not permission for every client to reach every target.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Public placement increases exposure and is not required for listener routing.

items.prompt: A zone impairment removes half the targets while long-lived requests remain active. What should the design include?
constraints: Long requests must have a bounded completion path.
New work should not use failed targets.
Remaining capacity must be protected from a retry storm.

options.text: Use target draining and bounded timeouts, retry only idempotent work, and protect surviving targets with connection and request limits.
Retry every active request immediately against every surviving target regardless of operation safety.
Keep failed targets registered until all connections eventually time out without a bound.
Return successful responses for interrupted requests so clients do not retry.

feedback.Reason: A zone failure requires both target removal and protection of the surviving capacity from unsafe retries.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Draining, bounded connection lifetimes, idempotency, and admission controls define how in-flight work and new requests behave.
Details.scenarioApplication: The service tells callers whether work completed, retries safe operations, and limits load on the remaining zone.
Details.errorCorrection: Unbounded retries can overload survivors, failed targets cannot finish useful work, and fake success corrupts client state.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Some long requests may fail during a zone event; the objective should define retry and recovery behavior.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Unsafe or unbounded retries can create duplicate work and overload survivors.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Unbounded draining delays removal of a failed target and consumes resources.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: A load balancer cannot truthfully succeed an interrupted operation.

items.prompt: An ALB is Multi-AZ but all targets write to a single zonal file server. What must change?
constraints: The file server is required for successful requests.
One zone failure is in scope.
The application needs shared file access.

options.text: Move the shared-file dependency to a multi-AZ or replicated service and validate mount, lock, throughput, and failover behavior with the target fleet.
Add more ALB targets in other zones without changing the file server.
Cache file reads in the ALB because load balancers automatically replicate backend files.
Use a second file path on the same server so the data has two locations.

feedback.Reason: A Multi-AZ front end cannot compensate for a required zonal storage dependency.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: The backend must provide shared data availability across the same failure domain as the serving fleet.
Details.scenarioApplication: The application continues or enters an explicit degraded mode when a zone is impaired, with file consistency and recovery tested.
Details.errorCorrection: More targets multiply calls to the failed file server, ALB does not store files, and two paths on one host share failure.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A managed file service or replicated storage adds cost and semantics that must fit the workload.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: More targets do not remove the zonal backend dependency.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: ALB is a traffic distributor and not a file cache.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Two paths on one server do not create independent storage failure domains.

items.prompt: A service needs to retain at least one healthy target in each of two zones during scale-in. Which capacity design supports this?
constraints: The group has multiple subnets.
The minimum healthy baseline is two targets.
Scale-in must not concentrate all capacity in one zone.

options.text: Set group minimum and placement behavior from the two-zone baseline, use health-aware target distribution, and test scale-in and zone-loss outcomes.
Set minimum capacity to one and trust the load balancer to create a target in the missing zone.
Use one instance with two network interfaces, one per zone.
Disable scale-in permanently so the original distribution is never evaluated.

feedback.Reason: Baseline capacity and placement policy must reflect the availability objective before scaling events occur.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Auto Scaling group bounds and subnet distribution determine how much healthy capacity remains during scale-in or failure.
Details.scenarioApplication: The team simulates normal scale-in and one-zone loss and confirms a target remains in the surviving zone with enough capacity.
Details.errorCorrection: Load balancers do not create targets, interfaces on one instance share failure, and disabling scale-in wastes resources rather than proving behavior.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A higher minimum protects availability but costs more during quiet periods.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: A load balancer cannot provision missing compute capacity.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: One instance remains one failure domain regardless of interfaces.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Avoiding scale-in does not prove the design handles capacity and failure behavior.

items.prompt: A TCP service needs static public IPs and target capacity in multiple Availability Zones. Which design should be evaluated?
constraints: The protocol is TCP.
Partners allow a fixed address set.
The service must tolerate a zone failure.

options.text: Use a Network Load Balancer with zonal static addresses or allocated addresses as required, targets in multiple zones, and health-aware failover behavior.
Use a single public EC2 address and add a second DNS name for the other zone.
Use an ALB path rule because static IPs are an HTTP-only feature.
Use one NLB target in each zone but place both listeners on one zonal subnet.

feedback.Reason: NLB provides transport forwarding and address behavior suitable for fixed TCP endpoints while distributing targets across zones.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: NLB listeners accept supported transport traffic and can expose stable addresses per enabled zone; target health controls routing.
Details.scenarioApplication: The team validates partner allowlists, target distribution, zone loss, source behavior, and connection recovery.
Details.errorCorrection: One host remains a SPOF, ALB path rules do not solve raw TCP addressing, and one NLB subnet concentrates the load-balancer failure domain.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Static addresses and transport pass-through preserve partner contracts but require explicit client and connection recovery behavior.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: DNS aliases do not create independent compute or static transport capacity.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Static transport addressing is not an HTTP path-routing decision.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: The load balancer itself must span the required zones, not only its targets.

items.prompt: A load-balanced service passes normal traffic tests but fails when one zone is removed. What was missing?
constraints: Normal traffic was distributed across all zones.
Remaining capacity was not tested.
The service objective applies during the failure.

options.text: Test the reduced-capacity state explicitly, including target warm-up, downstream connections, quotas, data access, latency, and retry behavior after one zone is impaired.
Add more targets everywhere without measuring the remaining-zone bottleneck.
Lower the service objective during the failure so the existing design passes.
Disable the zone health check so all target counts remain equal.

feedback.Reason: A Multi-AZ design must be sized and tested for the degraded state, not only the normal state.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Zone loss changes target count, connection concentration, downstream load, and capacity headroom.
Details.scenarioApplication: The team sets a tested baseline and either preserves the objective or exposes an explicit degraded state and recovery plan.
Details.errorCorrection: More unmeasured targets may overload dependencies, silently lowering the objective is misleading, and failed targets should not receive traffic.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Overprovisioning for a zone loss costs more but may be required by the availability objective.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Capacity must be validated against the degraded path and dependencies.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Changing the objective without an approved degraded contract hides failure.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Health checks are necessary to remove unusable targets.

items.prompt: Targets in two zones should accept traffic only from an ALB. Which security design is correct?
constraints: Targets are private.
The ALB is the only supported client path.
The rule must remain valid as target instances change.

options.text: Allow the target port from the ALB security group or equivalent trusted load-balancer source and deny direct client ingress.
Allow the target port from the entire VPC CIDR because all VPC clients are trusted.
Use one security group for the ALB, targets, and every application client.
Give each target a public IP and depend on the ALB to hide it.

feedback.Reason: A source security-group rule expresses the intended load-balancer-to-target boundary while allowing target replacement.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Security-group references follow the load-balancer identity rather than individual target addresses.
Details.scenarioApplication: Clients reach the ALB, the ALB reaches target ports, and direct target paths are not part of the supported architecture.
Details.errorCorrection: VPC CIDRs include unintended sources, one broad group weakens isolation, and public target IPs expand exposure.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Cross-account or cross-VPC designs may need different source controls but should preserve the same least-privilege boundary.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: A VPC CIDR is broader than the intended ALB source.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: One shared group creates broad trust between clients and targets.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: A public target address provides a bypass and larger attack surface.

items.prompt: An ALB and application fleet span two zones, but the database endpoint is reachable only through one zone's route. What remains?
constraints: The database is required for requests.
The application uses private routing.
A zone failure must not remove database reachability.

options.text: A zonal network path remains a dependency; use a Multi-AZ database endpoint and routing or connectivity design that survives the zone failure.
Nothing; the ALB can route database connections directly to another zone.
Add more application instances in the surviving zone without fixing the route.
Expose the database publicly so every zone can reach it.

feedback.Reason: A multi-AZ front end cannot overcome a critical zonal route or data endpoint dependency.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: The application path must include routes, security, DNS, and a database failover endpoint that remain usable after one zone fails.
Details.scenarioApplication: The team exercises zone loss and validates connection resolution, retries, database health, and remaining application capacity.
Details.errorCorrection: ALB does not proxy database connections, more app instances cannot repair a route, and public exposure is not a safe failover design.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Local versus cross-zone paths can affect cost and latency, but the availability objective defines the required behavior.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: An ALB routes application requests and does not repair database network paths.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: More application instances do not fix the critical route.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Public database exposure increases attack surface and does not create a managed failover endpoint.

items.prompt: A rolling deployment replaces targets across two zones. Which condition protects availability?
constraints: A minimum serving capacity must remain.
The new version needs health validation.
Draining can take time.

options.text: Replace targets in bounded batches while maintaining minimum healthy capacity across zones, draining connections, and stopping or rolling back on failed health or service objectives.
Terminate all targets in one zone and then the other before starting the new version.
Route all traffic to the first new target so its health is tested under full load.
Disable target health checks during deployment so new instances are counted immediately.

feedback.Reason: A Multi-AZ rolling deployment preserves healthy capacity while the new version proves itself.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Batch size, minimum healthy targets, draining, and health checks constrain the deployment blast radius.
Details.scenarioApplication: The team verifies each zone and target group before continuing and keeps a rollback path for the previous version.
Details.errorCorrection: Replacing one zone at a time can remove the entire remaining margin, one target cannot absorb full load safely, and disabled health hides failure.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Safer deployment can require surge capacity and longer rollout time.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Removing a full zone before replacement can violate the availability objective.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: One unproven target is a bottleneck and single failure boundary.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Health checks are necessary to count usable capacity.

items.prompt: A Multi-AZ ALB routes requests to stateless application instances, but login sessions are local to each target. What is the availability defect?
constraints: Any target may receive the next request.
A zone or instance failure is in scope.
Users must not lose authentication state unexpectedly.

options.text: Externalize session state or use a carefully governed token so target and zone replacement does not make authentication depend on one instance.
Enable long-lived stickiness and call the session path Multi-AZ even when one target fails.
Copy session memory to every target after each request without versioning.
Disable ALB health checks so the original session target remains reachable during failure.

feedback.Reason: A multi-AZ load balancer cannot preserve local session memory after target or zone failure.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Shared session storage or verifiable tokens make target replacement independent from authentication state.
Details.scenarioApplication: The service defines expiry, revocation, consistency, and failure behavior and tests a request routed to another zone.
Details.errorCorrection: Stickiness masks rather than removes local state, unversioned memory copying can lose updates, and disabled health routes to failed targets.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: External sessions add a dependency while tokens add revocation and claim freshness decisions.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Affinity does not survive target or zone failure and reduces distribution.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Ad hoc copying does not guarantee consistency or recovery completeness.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Failed targets should be removed, not preserved for local memory.

items.prompt: A service adds a third Availability Zone but cannot create the required load-balancer IPs or targets due to quotas. What should happen before rollout?
constraints: The design depends on three zones.
Quotas are account and Region specific.
The service needs tested capacity in the new zone.

options.text: Check and raise required quotas, subnet IP capacity, target limits, and downstream capacity before adding the zone, then validate the full rollout.
Add the zone in production and assume quotas increase when the load balancer needs them.
Use one target in the new zone without checking health because any third zone improves availability.
Remove the existing zones so the new zone has all available quota.

feedback.Reason: A new failure domain is useful only if the services can actually provision and serve capacity there.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Subnet addresses, load-balancer limits, instance quotas, and downstream capacity constrain a Multi-AZ expansion.
Details.scenarioApplication: The team preflights resource creation and performs a zone-loss test after the new placement is active.
Details.errorCorrection: Quotas do not automatically increase, one untested target is not meaningful redundancy, and removing existing zones reduces resilience.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Quota headroom and additional zones add planning and cost but protect scale and failure recovery.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Quota exhaustion can block the intended expansion or recovery.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: A target must be healthy and capacity-tested to add useful resilience.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Removing established capacity can worsen the failure domain while adding uncertain capacity.

items.prompt: A Multi-AZ service has one aggregate latency alarm and cannot distinguish a zone-specific target failure. What observability should be added?
constraints: Zone and target identity are available.
Operators need to act before remaining capacity fails.
The service objective includes tail latency and errors.

options.text: Break down health, latency, errors, capacity, connection, and request metrics by Availability Zone and target, and correlate them with routing and dependency signals.
Remove zone dimensions because aggregate metrics are always less noisy and more actionable.
Alarm only on database CPU because the database is the only shared dependency.
Wait for all targets to fail before paging so the zone pattern is unambiguous.

feedback.Reason: Zone-level observability reveals loss of capacity and traffic concentration before the remaining fleet is exhausted.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Dimensions by zone and target connect health and utilization to the failure domain and routing change.
Details.scenarioApplication: Operators can shift traffic, restore capacity, or activate a degraded mode based on the affected zone and dependency.
Details.errorCorrection: Aggregate-only metrics hide the failure, database CPU misses target problems, and waiting for total failure is too late.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: High-cardinality metrics need cost and retention control, but the failure objective requires actionable dimensions.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Removing dimensions hides the exact failure domain operators need.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: The database is not the only cause of target or routing failure.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Paging after total failure violates early detection and recovery objectives.

items.prompt: After one zone fails, the ALB sends twice the normal traffic to the surviving targets and the database reaches its connection limit. What control is needed?
constraints: The surviving target fleet is healthy but smaller.
The database has finite connections.
The service must fail safely rather than overload the data tier.

options.text: Use connection pooling or a proxy, bounded request concurrency, queueing or explicit admission control, and a degraded behavior sized for zone-loss capacity.
Add unlimited retries at the ALB so every request eventually reaches the database.
Disable health checks in the failed zone so traffic is distributed back to unavailable targets.
Increase database connections without testing memory, locks, or the remaining service objective.

feedback.Reason: Zone-loss concentration can overload downstream dependencies, so the remaining path needs explicit backpressure and connection protection.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Pooling, proxies, and bounded concurrency prevent application scale and failover routing from exceeding database capacity.
Details.scenarioApplication: The service queues or rejects work honestly when the degraded capacity cannot satisfy all demand and alerts on queue age or errors.
Details.errorCorrection: Retries amplify database pressure, failed targets cannot provide capacity, and arbitrary connection increases can worsen resource exhaustion.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A degraded mode may reduce throughput or freshness but protects correctness and recovery.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Unbounded retries amplify load against a saturated database.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Unavailable targets do not provide useful failover capacity.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Increasing connections without testing can exhaust memory and worsen contention.

items.prompt: A new version causes errors only in one zone after a rolling deployment. Which rollback approach limits the blast radius?
constraints: The old version remains available in some targets.
The ALB can route by target health or deployment strategy.
Rollback must not remove all capacity.

options.text: Stop the rollout, drain or remove unhealthy new targets, restore the previous version in bounded batches, and verify service health across zones before continuing.
Replace every target immediately with the same new version so all zones are consistent.
Disable health checks to keep the new targets registered until the bug is fixed.
Send all traffic to the failing zone so its behavior is easier to observe in production.

feedback.Reason: A bounded rollback preserves serving capacity and removes the known-bad target path without expanding the failure.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Target health, draining, batch replacement, and previous artifacts allow the deployment to return to a known-good state.
Details.scenarioApplication: The team isolates the zone-specific issue, restores version consistency safely, and checks dependencies before full recovery.
Details.errorCorrection: Fleet-wide replacement expands impact, disabled health routes users to bad code, and traffic concentration in the failing zone worsens risk.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Rollback can leave mixed versions temporarily, so compatibility and state migration contracts must be designed.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Immediate fleet replacement increases outage blast radius.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Health checks should remove failing targets rather than hide them.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Sending traffic to a known-failing zone increases user impact.

items.prompt: Which evidence is strongest for approving a Multi-AZ load-balanced architecture?
constraints: The named failure is one Availability Zone loss.
The data and dependencies are included.
RTO, capacity, and correctness are measurable.

options.text: A controlled zone-loss test showing healthy routing, remaining capacity, state access, downstream limits, observability, and recovery within the service objective.
A diagram showing an ALB icon connected to two subnets without a failure test.
A successful normal-load test where every zone is healthy.
A promise that managed services handle availability without checking client or quota behavior.

feedback.Reason: The approval claim is about degraded runtime behavior, so evidence must exercise the failure and end-to-end request path.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: A test connects topology to target health, state, routes, capacity, dependencies, and recovery timing.
Details.scenarioApplication: The team records the observed RTO and residual gaps before accepting the architecture.
Details.errorCorrection: A diagram and normal-load test omit the failure path, and managed service claims do not replace application and quota validation.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Failure testing requires controls and cost but provides material evidence for the availability claim.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Topology alone does not prove target and dependency behavior during zone loss.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: A healthy normal path does not validate the degraded capacity path.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Managed services still have contracts and application-side recovery behavior to verify.
